tossups.text: At Serchina, a rebellion by this type of people was defeated by Crassus and Pompey. Olaudah Equiano discussed their life in his Interesting Narrative . A group of these people called Helots worked the fields of Sparta to allow citizens to spend their whole time focused on war. The American Colonization Society settled a group of these people in Liberia. For 10 points, name this type of person, some of whom were led to freedom by Harriet Tubman on the Underground Railroad.

This work defines the confina of humor and irony, and its second section describes the love of Don Giovanni as "not faithful but totally faithless," loving "not one but all." Published under the name Victor Eremita, its opening volume includes the sections "Silhouettes," "The Unhappiest One," and "The Seducer's Diary," the latter possibly based on the author's broken engagement to Regine Olsen. The title concept is in contrast to the synthesis of Hegel and creates the distinction between the aesthetic and the ethical. For 10 points, name this work of Soren Kierkegaard.

This polity's Louis I was succeeded by Queen Hedwig during the House of Anjou's brief rule over it. A ruler of this polity known as "[this polity's] Justinian" was succeeded by an expansionist king known as "the Elbow-High." The succession of this polity was governed for years by the Henrician Articles, named for this polity's short-reigned ruler who became Henry III of France. The provisions of Nihil novi and the liberum veto helped govern this polity's legislature which was governed by the 3 May Constitution. This country, which was [emphasize] invaded in the Deluge, was governed by a legislature called the Sejm ("same"). For 10 points, name this Eastern European country which was partitioned three times and is governed from Warsaw.

This thinker posited that a list of a substance's predications make up a complete notion of the substance. His namesake law states that if two objects have exactly the same properties, then they are the same object. Those ideas are his Predicate-in-Notion Principle and his concept of the Identity of Indiscernibles. He posited the existence of simple substances that interact with each other via the Principle of Pre-Established Harmony; said substances also being nonextendable, indivisible, and windowless. This author of Discourse on Metaphysics stated that everything happens for a reason, which is his Principle of Sufficient Reason. For 10 points, name this author of Monadology, who asserted that God must have created the best of all possible worlds in his Theodicy.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for blood types and rh factor. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this erythrocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The erythrocyte is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in blood types and rh factor.

tossups.text: In this country, women participated in the March of the Empty Pots to protest a leader who was protected from coups by the Schneider Doctrine. A regime in this country was embarrassed by a traffic incident in which a general shot at a woman who was mocking him. Carlos Prats helped put down the Tank Putsch in this country. The Rettig Report exposed the atrocities committed by this country's DINA secret police. A dictator from this country employed the Chicago Boys as economic advisors and mobilized the Caravan of Death after overthrowing Salvador Allende in a 1973 coup. For 10 points, name this South American country once ruled by Augusto Pinochet.

Along with Paul Hollander, this man published "The Murder They Heard" about the murder of Kitty Genovese, while his studies on "The Familiar Stranger: An Aspect of Urban Anonymity" appeared in Psychology Today. He worked with cameras in the works "Candid Camera" and "Image-Freezing Machine, and his "small world experiment" gave rise to the notion of six degrees of separation. He published Obedience and Authority: An Experimental View to describe variations of an experiment he conducted at Yale in 1961. For 10 points, name this psychologist whose most famous experiment saw its participants willingly obey orders to administer 450-volt shocks.

This god was sometimes called Ipalnemohuani, meaning, "by whom we live." One story claims that he burned himself to death after his rival got him to drunkenly seduce a celibate priestess and subsequently became the morning star. Another story claims that he floated away on a raft of snakes. This god, said to have created mankind from the bones of previous races and blood from his penis, had a twin brother named Xolotl, and his rival was the one-footed "smoking mirror" god Tezcatlipoca. For 10 points, name this "feathered serpent" god from Aztec mythology.

One ruler of this dynasty killed his childhood friend by hitting him with a game board, and this dynasty's Emperor Jing dealt with the Rebellion of the Seven States. This dynasty, which underwent a massive expansion under Emperor Wudi, was founded by Liu Bang. This dynasty was cut into two periods after Wang Mang created the Xin Dynasty. The Taoist Zhang Jue led an insurrection against this dynasty that was put down by its general Cao Cao, that was the Yellow Turban Rebellion. For 10 points, name this Chinese dynasty that ruled until 200 A.D. and shares its name with the predominant ethnic group of China.

To avoid humiliation, one leader of this country requested Julian Byng hold a new election, sparking a constitutional crisis. During a debate, a leader of this country was told "You had an option, sir" regarding his "patronage appointments." One leader of this country invoked its War Measures Act after the kidnapping of James Cross and Pierre Laporte. A proposed flag of this country was derided as the "Pearson Pennant". In 1995, Jean Chrétien oversaw over an independence referendum in this country, which had three separate governments under William Lyon Mackenzie King. For 10 points, name this country where Justin Trudeau governs from Ottawa.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for memory cells. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this T cell-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The T cell is a key component of the Immune system, involved in memory cells.

tossups.text: An institute dedicated to this man's thought was once partly led by James Hillman, whose popular book The Soul's Code mainly draws from this man's ideas. The original mission of the Bollingen Institute was to disperse the ideas of this thinker, who once collaborated with a statistician to examine hundreds of horoscopes of married couples to look for an "acausal connecting principle" that would explain parapsychology. This theorizer of "synchronicity" developed a theory that sought to explain why figures like the shadow, the wise old man, and the trickster are so common in folklore. Joseph Campbell's The Hero with a Thousand Faces cites the theory of archetypes advanced by, for 10 points, what Swiss psychologist who theorized the collective unconscious?

A trumpet call at the end of this composition's first movement falls from E to E-flat and abruptly shifts into a minor key. That movement's main theme is repeated by pizzicato strings in its Landler second movement. Its third movement opens with two sharp timpani notes, and sixteenth notes represent the subject of St. Anthony's sermon to the fish, while offstage trumpets and French horns are incorporated into the final movement entitled "Primal Light." This work's first movement was originally the symphonic poem Totenfeier, and poems written by Friedrich Klopstock are used for its Auferstehung choral movement. For 10 points, name this symphony preceded by "Titan," a work of Gustav Mahler.
acceptableAnswers: Mahler’s Symphony No. 2 in C minor

tossups.text: One type of these bodies ceases to emit radiation at the so-called "death line." A 2017 multi-messenger astronomy breakthrough involved measuring both gravitational waves and a gamma-ray burst from the merger of two of these bodies, known as a kilonova. An upper limit on these bodies' mass is named for Tolman, Oppenheimer, and Volkov. A "glitch" is a small increase in the frequency emitted by rapidly rotating examples of these bodies called pulsars. Stars whose mass is just above the Chandrasekar limit form one of these bodies after a supernova instead of a white dwarf. For 10 points, what extremely dense celestial bodies are named for a subatomic particle?

A number of sepoys revolted against this dynasty in the Ispah Rebellion on account of ethnic strife in the city of Zaitun ("zye-TOON"). A syncretic version of Islam was promoted to help pacify this dynasty's borderlands by its minister Sayyid Shams al-Din Omar. The nickname "He who fled from the taruk," or Turks, was given to the Burmese king Narathihapate ("nuh-rah-thee-hah-puh-tay") after he refused to fight an invasion by this dynasty's governor Nasr al-Din. Two "commanders of ten thousand" are credited with murdering this dynasty's corrupt Uzbek minister Ahmad al-Fanakati. The semu ("suh-moo") caste provided most of the staff of this dynasty's Grand Secretariat. Its "four-class" system heavily favored foreigners, such as Turks and Persians, driving the resentment behind its overthrow in the Red Turban Rebellion. For 10 points, name this dynasty which brought foreigners to its capital of Shangdu, or Xanadu, where Marco Polo visited its ruler Khubilai Khan.

In 1603, an ice floe destroyed this city's first permanent bridge, which had connected it to the jurydyka of Praga. In 1794, a shoemaker named Jan Kilinski led the armed peasantry of this city against the occupying Russian Empire. This city was the primary meeting place of the Sejm [sehm] until permanently established there in 1949. Jürgen Stroop helped put down an uprising in this city's Ghetto, eventually sending most of the rebels to Treblinka and other death camps. For 10 points, name this city of on the Vistula River, the capital of Poland.

This president called for federal anti-lynching protections in a speech outlining the creation of the President's Committee for Civil Rights. The Supreme Court ruled this president's seizure of steel production facilities unconstitutional in the Youngstown Steel case. This president vetoed the Taft-Hartley Act as part of his Fair Deal, but was overridden by the Do-Nothing Congress. Despite the walkout of Strom Thurmond and several other Southern delegates at the Democratic National Convention, this president still won the 1948 election against Thomas Dewey. For 10 points, name this Democratic president who succeeded Franklin D. Roosevelt.

Modern students of this instrument often study with a large red book which contains a famously difficult arrangement of The Carnival of Venice. That book is Arban's Complete Conservatory Method for [this instrument]. It's not the trombone, but students of this instrument are told to extend a certain slide when playing a low D or any note involving the third valve. The range of this B flat instrument is typically from the F sharp below middle C up to the C two octaves above middle C. For 10 points, name this three-valved brass instrument that is smaller than a French horn, the modern-day successor of the bugle.

This economist is the second namesake of social welfare functions in which an individual's utility is based solely on the goods allocated to that individual, and which are contrasted with Arrow social welfare functions. This man argued that one method of producing champagne could be most profitable at both high and low interest rates, but not in between, as part of his reswitching argument during the Cambridge Capital Controversy. He introduced the theory of using what a consumer purchases to infer their utility function; that is revealed preference theory. This economist pioneered using constrained optimization problems to model economic situations in his book Foundations of Economic Analysis. For 10 points, name this first American to win the Nobel Prize in Economics, the author of the 1948 textbook Economics.

This author described people stealing body parts from the hospital of Gong of Four member Dr. Menka in Chronicles from the Land of the Happiest People on Earth. People like the sculptor Sekoni return home in this author's The Interpreters. A character created by this author calls his father an "eater of leftovers." A praise singer is told the story of the "Not I" bird in a play by this author, in which Simon Pilkings fails to stop Elesin from committing suicide. For 10 points, name this Nigerian author of Death and the King's Horseman.

parts.text: Name this 1925 trial in Tennessee regarding a high school teacher's violation of the Butler Act.

The Scopes "monkey" trial was a debate over the teaching of this scientific concept in public schools, which the Butler Act restricted. "Intelligent design" was promoted as an alternative to this concept until a 2005 court case.

On the seventh day of the Scopes trial, Darrow called Bryan to the stand as an expert witness for the historical nature of this book. All of the ensuing testimony was stricken from the record as unrelated to the case.

bonuses.leadin: This event was manufactured as a publicity stunt for a religious debate, and it attracted Clarence Darrow and William Jennings Bryan as participants. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this Scottish philosopher, who also wrote an Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding.
Hume later repudiated this first major philosophical work of his, a 1739 book divided into three sections on understanding, passions, and feelings.
Failing to win renown as a philosopher, Hume switched genres and won fame for this six-volume work, which concludes with a discussion of the Glorious Revolution.

bonuses.leadin: Because he was afraid of a poor reception, this man didn't publish his Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion during his life. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this "reckless" Englishman who was killed at the Battle of Shrewsbury in 1403.
Henry Percy rebelled against this king, a son of John of Gaunt who succeeded Richard II.
Henry IV founded this house, which fought the House of York in the Wars of the Roses.

bonuses.leadin: This man and his father, the 1st Earl of Northumberland, led England to victory over Scotland, led by Archibald Douglas, 4th Earl of Douglas, at the Battle of Humbleton Hill. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Catholic movement that began in Latin America and aimed to provide assistance to the poor. The name of this movement was coined by Gustavo Gutiérrez.
As a cardinal in the '80s, this pope sharply criticized the growing Marxist influence of liberation theology on the Catholic Church. He was succeeded by Pope Francis after he resigned in 2013.

The teachings of liberation theology often stress the need to provide one of these specific things for the poor. Upon coming into office, Pope Francis used this specific phrase in his 2013 address Evangelii gaudium.

bonuses.leadin: In Brazil, this movement gave rise to units called Base Ecclesial Communities, in which a clergy member was responsible for addressing community needs. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with parathyroid hormone.
What is the main function of the thyroid in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to parathyroid hormone.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Identify this league, made up of Norway, Sweden, and Denmark.
The Kalmar Union was founded by this woman, who proclaimed Eric of Pomerania to be the King of Norway, and later Denmark and Sweden.

Eric of Pomerania was the grandson of this extremely unpopular Swedish King, under whose tutelage Margaret I grew up. This man successfully invaded Sweden, but was later defeated and deposed at the Battle of Asle.

bonuses.leadin: This ended after a series of executions in Stortorget Square, which was known as the Stockholm Bloodbath. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these things that include the sequence of instruction, reading materials on a syllabus, and resources for school subjects. A CV, named for these things and "vitae," lists a person's educational and research experiences.
This thinker's The Modularity of Mind revived a critical component of curriculum studies called faculty psychology, which asserted that the brain could be strengthened through memorization.
This author's book The School and Society proposed student-centered curricula that involved children's natural interests, drawing from experiments at his University of Chicago Laboratory Schools.

bonuses.leadin: A field of study named for these things included a school called the Herbartians, who believed that memorizing isolated facts had little importance on the educational outcomes of students. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this woman from Greek mythology, who was tormented by Hera and watched over by Argus Panoptes because of this woman's relationship with Zeus.

After this woman had an affair with Zeus, Hera took the completely reasonable response of turning her into a snake and then cursing her to never be able to close her eyes right before slaughtering all of this woman's children.
Because this nymph kept distracting Hera while Zeus was up to no good, Hera laid a curse on this nymph that prevented her from communicating with the object of her love, Narcissus.

bonuses.leadin: The Bosphorus strait was named for this woman after she crossed it while being chased by a stinging gadfly. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this African-American civil rights leader, who was convinced by Elijah Muhammad to join the political and religious group Nation of Islam.

In justifying the "chickens coming home to roost" comment, Malcolm cited the death of this civil rights leader. This NAACP field secretary was murdered in Mississippi by Klansman Byron De La Beckwith.

This Malcolm X speech compares taking civil rights cases to the federal government to "running from the wolf to the fox," and speaks of "the type of Black man on the scene in America today... who just doesn't intend to turn the other cheek any longer."

bonuses.leadin: In one speech, this man called the assassination of President John F. Kennedy "chickens coming home to roost." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this dynasty which was conquered in a conflict during which a river supposedly ran black and red with ink and blood. Harun al-Rashid founded the House of Wisdom during the rule of this dynasty.
That conquest was by this empire under the leadership of Hulagu Khan. Other leaders of this empire include Genghis Khan.

Hulagu's advance was finally stopped at this 1260 battle after he left only 10,000 men in the Levant to continue his conquest. That force under Kitbuga was almost entirely destroyed by Mamluk sultan Qutuz at this battle.

bonuses.leadin: This dynasty sacked the Byzantine city of Amorium. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with neuron structure.
What is the main function of the axon in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to neuron structure.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.

parts.text: This Canadian author of American Capitalism wrote about how the private sector became wealthy but the public sector remained poor in the United States after World War II in his work The Affluent Society.
Some believe that Galbraith in his Affluent Society is denouncing this type of market, championed by Adam Smith in his Wealth of Nations.
This group was led by economist Francois Quesnay, and they believed that agricultural labor was the only type that was valuable. They contrasted sharply with the mercantilists.

bonuses.leadin: For ten points each, name these other economists.

parts.text: Identify this painting of a pipe with an inscription which translates as "this is not a pipe."
The Treachery of Images was painted by this Belgian surrealist, who also painted Golconda and TimeTransfixed.
This other Magritte work features the iconic image of a man in a bowler hat whose face is hidden by an apple, supposedly a self-portrait

bonuses.leadin: The artist argued that what he wrote on his painting was correct because the image was only a representation. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these particles. That result was later explained by these particles' oscillations between electron, muon, and tau flavors.
The sun releases neutrinos as a byproduct of stellar nucleosynthesis, which is a type of this reaction in which atoms are combined to make atoms of different elements.

If the complex phase angle governing neutrino oscillations is not a multiple of pi, then this phenomenon would result. This phenomenon may be responsible for the universe containing more matter than antimatter.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on answers that do not include “violation”

bonuses.leadin: The Homestake experiment counted only one third of the expected number of these particles emitted by the sun. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this last name of Laurent-Desire, who became the leader of his country in 1997, and his son Joseph, who took power after his father was assassinated in 2001 by a former child soldier.
Laurent-Desire Kabila ousted Mobutu Sese Seko to become the leader of this country, formerly known as Zaire.

During his tenure, Mobutu enacted a state campaign with this name against Western culture. Under this policy, Leopoldville was renamed Kinshasa and Western suits were banned and replaced by the abacost.

bonuses.leadin: Yoweri Museveni and Paul Kagame helped one leader with this last name seize power, before invading again the next year in an attempt to overthrow him. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name these indigenous people who fought the Spanish in the Arauco ("a-rocko") War under leaders like Caupolicán ("cow-po-li-kahn") and Lautaro. ("lao-ta-ro").
The Mapuche inhabit land in what is now Chile and this country. The "good winds" that allowed sailors to safely travel to this country's capital city inspired its name, Buenos Aires.
Like many other native people, the Mapuche intermingled with settlers to form this general class of people. This term generally referred to those of mixed white and native ancestry.

bonuses.leadin: After having both of his hands cut off, a chief of these people named Galvarino went into battle fighting with knives tied to his wrist stumps. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this country formerly ruled by Siad Barre, with capital Mogadishu.
Much of southern Somalia is now under the control of this Islamic militant group, allegedly with the support of Eritrea. Its name means "the youth."

This region of Somalia declared autonomy in 1998, and its capital is Bosaso. It has engaged in border conflicts at Sool and Sanaag with Somaliland. It has also become the base for many Indian Ocean pirates.

bonuses.leadin: This country was briefly ruled by the Islamic Courts Union until Ethiopia intervened with force, in support of the Transitional Federal Government. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Black dance style that blends aspects of forms like tap and break. The taps of a pair of dancing twins are featured on several tracks of a 2022 rap album titled "Mr. Morale and the Big" practitioners of this style.
acceptableAnswers: accept Mr. Morale and the Big Steppers

parts.text: Mr. Morale and the Big Steppers was this artist's first LP since his Pulitzer-winning album DAMN.

A Black dance called Pattin' Juba or hamboning is often cited as influencing this musician's namesake clave ("KLAH-vay") beat, which is often described as a "syncopated 3-2." "I'm a Man" was the B-side to the namesake song of this musician, who often played a rectangular guitar.

bonuses.leadin: Competitions for this dance exhibit signature styles of Greek organizations at historically Black colleges and universities, as depicted in the film Stomp the Yard. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this problem in which one state increasing its security may cause other states to become frightened and increase their military capabilities, which makes the first state less safe than before.

The security dilemma is a favorite of Realist international scholars who believe that the international stage is defined by this term. When this term is applied to domestic politics, it means a lack of government.

Proponents of Liberalism in IR argue that realist theories on war especially do not apply between states that have this form of government, though notable counterexamples include the participants in the Kargil War.

bonuses.leadin: This problem may result in states being trapped in an arms race in which they spend more on defense while not gaining a relative advantage. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this genre of the texts which serve as epigraphs for a 1989 novel by Laura Esquivel.

In Like Water for Chocolate, Tita bakes a vomit-inducing cake, but cooks much better food for the wedding of this daughter of Rosaura. A different character with this first name begrudgingly looks after her sister Nenny in The House on Mango Street.
Tita's family lives in the north of this country. Children and parents leaving this country for one to the north are separated from each other in Valeria Luiselli's 2019 novel Lost Children Archive.

bonuses.leadin: Each chapter opens with one of these texts in a novel where Tita's sister Rosaura dies from excessive flatulence. For 10 points each:
